title: Winning the first conversation

slides.title: Winning the first conversation
slides.body:
Introduce yourself.
Offer a showing.
Listen to the buyer.

Today’s practiceMake a first call and agree on a showing.Work with a partner. Give specific feedback. Try again.
slides.notes: Invite a recent example from one person, then begin. Keep the opening to two minutes.
slides.cue: Ask: What would you like to get better at today?

slides.title: What is the buyer trying to do?
slides.lead: They asked about a home. Begin there.
slides.body:
“Hi, I asked about 1234 Lane. Can I see it this weekend?”

Which response helps them first?
slides.notes: Ask everyone to vote. Invite someone to describe a time a sales call felt like an interview. Keep examples to one sentence.
slides.cue: What would make this buyer want to keep talking?

slides.title: Call promptly after accepting the lead
slides.lead: Aim to call within ten minutes when the contact has not already been made.
slides.body:
Read the context

Check the property, request, and recent contact activity.

Respect the situation

A live connection, agreed call time, or request for text changes the next step.

Keep the call brief

About five minutes is a useful target. Learn enough to help and agree on a showing.
slides.notes: This timing comes from the supplied training. Use the team’s actual notification workflow. Do not place a duplicate call while someone is already speaking with the buyer.
slides.cue: What would you check before dialing?

slides.title: Use LEAD on the first call
slides.lead: Offer the appointment early, then learn what matters to the buyer.
slides.body:
L

Lead

Name, brokerage, Zillow connection, and reason for calling.

E

Extend

Offer two showing options early.

A

Ask

Ask permission, then listen and follow up.

D

Deliver

Summarize what you heard and confirm the plan.
slides.notes: Use Eric’s LEAD order. An early invitation is the default; respond to an urgent question or the actual situation when needed. Do not insert qualification questions before the invitation.
slides.cue: Say the four letters and what each asks you to do.

slides.title: Introduce yourself in about ten seconds
slides.lead: Include your name, brokerage, Zillow connection, and the property.
slides.body: “Hi Jordan, I’m Sam with Northside Realty, a featured agent on Zillow. I’m calling about your request to see 1234 Lane.”
slides.notes: Model it once, then have partners say it three times without reading. Listen for all four details. Keep it conversational; do not reward speed alone.
slides.cue: Which detail helps the buyer recognize this call?

slides.title: Offer two showing times
slides.lead: Make it easy for the buyer to answer.
slides.body:
Start with two options

“Would Saturday morning or afternoon work better?”

If neither works

“What time would work for you?”

If they ask a question

Answer what you know, clarify what you need to check, then return to the invitation.
slides.notes: Have one partner accept, one decline both times, then one ask a property question. Let the agent respond to the situation without restarting the whole script.
slides.cue: Practice each response with your partner.

slides.title: Ask permission and listen
slides.lead: Learn why this home caught their attention.
slides.body:
Permission

“Can I ask what caught your eye about this one?”

Follow the answer

“You mentioned the yard. What would you like to use the space for?”

Listen for the need

Ask a useful follow-up instead of running through a fixed list.
slides.notes: Use the buyer’s stated preferences. Do not infer family circumstances or steer based on personal characteristics. Practice one follow-up question that uses the buyer’s exact words.
slides.cue: What would you ask after “I need a quieter space to work”?

slides.title: Save financial screening for the right conversation
slides.lead: The first showing invitation does not depend on pre-approval.
slides.body: The buyer wants to see the home. What belongs on this first call?
slides.notes: State the distinction once. Do not teach agents to ignore questions the buyer voluntarily raises. Acknowledge and arrange the appropriate help.
slides.cue: What can you learn without screening the buyer?

slides.title: Summarize the buyer’s words and the plan
slides.body: “You want a quieter place to work, and the yard on Lane caught your eye. We’re set for Saturday at 10. I’ll confirm access and send the address. Have I missed anything?”
slides.notes: Ask the buyer role to correct one detail. The agent should acknowledge the correction and update the plan. A summary is not an invitation to add a sales pitch.
slides.cue: What would you put into the contact note?

slides.title: Answer the question honestly
slides.lead: Be clear about your role and what you still need to check.
slides.body:
“Are you the listing agent?”

If you are not: “No. I’m a buyer’s agent. I can help arrange a showing and get answers about the home.”

“How old is the roof?”

“I don’t have that confirmed yet. I’ll check the available information and get back to you.”

“Is it still available?”

Share the status you have verified. If you need to check, say so and follow up.
slides.notes: Do not imply a relationship with the listing agent that does not exist. Never hide known property status to obtain an appointment. Ask the room to improve an evasive answer.
slides.cue: What would you say if you do not know the answer?

slides.title: If the home is under contract
slides.lead: Tell the buyer what you know, then discuss what is still possible.
slides.body: “That home is under contract. I’ll confirm whether backup offers or showings are being considered. What interested you about it? I can also look for similar homes.”
slides.notes: Use truthful status plus a useful next step. Do not promise access, availability, or that a contract will fall through. Let the buyer decide whether alternatives are useful.
slides.cue: Which part answers the question directly?

slides.title: Practice the opening and invitation
slides.body:
Round 1 · Buyer is ready

Introduce yourself and offer two showing times.

Round 2 · Buyer asks about the home

Answer what you know or explain what you will check. Return to scheduling when appropriate.

Round 3 · Times do not work

Find an option that does. Confirm the next step.
slides.notes: Give each agent 30 seconds per round and 30 seconds of feedback. Repeat only the part that needs work. Do not let the observer coach during the attempt.
slides.cue: Name one specific phrase that helped the buyer.

slides.title: Ask a follow-up that fits the answer
slides.lead: Use a different buyer response each time.
slides.body:
“The commute.”

“The separate workspace.”

“I liked the outdoor space.”
slides.notes: Partners choose a response without telling the agent. The agent asks permission and one follow-up. Ask the buyer whether the question helped them explain their need.
slides.cue: Did you follow the answer, or change the subject?

slides.title: Run the whole first call
slides.lead: Agent, buyer, observer. Rotate so everyone makes a call.
slides.notes: Allow 1 minute for roles. Each round: 3-minute call, 1-minute feedback, 1-minute retry. Rotate three times. If pairs, the buyer gives feedback and both complete a call. Fictional case details are practice material.
slides.cue: Observer: describe what you heard, then request one retry.

slides.title: If they do not answer
slides.lead: Leave a brief voicemail and set the next task.
slides.body:
“Hi Jordan, this is Sam with Northside Realty, a featured Zillow agent. I’m calling about 1234 Lane. Would this afternoon or tomorrow morning work for a quick call? You can reach me at [number].”

Text can support the call

“Hi Jordan, Sam with Northside Realty here about your Zillow request for 1234 Lane. Is now a good time for a quick call?”

Update the record

Record the attempt accurately and schedule the next personal attempt.
slides.notes: Have each agent leave a 20-second voicemail. Use their actual callback number in real calls. Text is useful for logistics; move detailed property or financing discussion to a call.
slides.cue: Does the message explain who you are and why you called?

slides.title: Make at least five personal attempts in the first seven days
slides.body:
What counts

A personal call, including a voicemail, or a personal text.

What does not count

Automated messages and emails do not count toward the five.

What happens after a week

Continue based on the buyer’s situation and team process. Day seven is not a stop rule.
slides.notes: This uses Eric’s current doctrine. Remove the original implication that later effort is wasted. Ask an agent to distinguish an automated touch from a personal attempt. Do not invent a new cadence beyond the first week.
slides.cue: Which attempts would you count in a contact history?

slides.title: Explain LEAD without looking back
slides.lead: Write first. Compare with a partner. Then check.
slides.body:
Check the order
Lead with who you are. Extend the invitation early. Ask permission and listen. Deliver a summary and confirm the plan.
slides.notes: Allow 45 seconds without notes. Ask a partner to identify one missing detail. Have the agent redo that part aloud.
slides.cue: Where does the showing invitation belong?

slides.title: Before your next client conversation
slides.lead: Write down when you will practice again.
slides.body:
After the call

Save the true stage, a useful note, and the next dated task.

Within 24 hours

Make a practice call without reading a script.

With your coach

Review one first call for LEAD order and a clear agreed next step.
slides.notes: Ask each agent to name one behavior they will practice. Within 24 hours, ask them to explain it without notes. In three days, use a new scenario. In seven days, review an actual example. These are suggested coaching intervals; no reminders are sent.
slides.cue: Tell your partner what you will practice and when.

cases.name: Jordan · weekend showing
cases.quote: “I asked about Lane because I need a quieter space to work. Saturday morning might work.”
cases.goal: Buyer: ask whether the agent is the listing agent. Agent: use LEAD and answer honestly.

cases.name: Morgan · property question
cases.quote: “Before I book anything, do you know how old the roof is?”
cases.goal: Buyer: accept another time if the first two do not work. Agent: say what you know, capture what needs checking, and offer a visit.

cases.name: Alex · home unavailable
cases.quote: “I only called about that one home. Is it still available?”
cases.goal: Practice fact: the home is under contract. Tell the buyer promptly and ask whether similar homes would help.
